comment: Root certificates of the time-stamp authorities used by PolicyGate's reference deployment, as pins for verify-evidence.py --tsa-roots. A pin is the SHA-256 of the root certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo (DER): openssl x509 -in root.pem -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER | sha256sum. An auditor should not take these pins on trust: compare each root with the one the authority itself publishes, recompute the pin, and keep an own copy of this file. The verifier never trusts certificates found inside a pack.

roots.name: freetsa
roots.subject: O=Free TSA, OU=Root CA, CN=www.freetsa.org, emailAddress=busilezas@gmail.com, L=Wuerzburg, ST=Bayern, C=DE
roots.obtained: 2026-11-07 from https://freetsa.org/files/cacert.pem; that file's SHA-256 2151b61137ffa86bf664691ba67e7da0b19f98c758e3d228d5d8ebf27e044438 equals the value published on https://freetsa.org/index_en.php. The same certificate is inside every FreeTSA response requested with certReq=true.
roots.check: curl -sS https://freetsa.org/files/cacert.pem -o freetsa-root.pem; sha256sum freetsa-root.pem; compare with the page; then compute the pin. FreeTSA's own root, not in browser trust stores.

roots.name: sectigo
roots.subject: C=GB, O=Sectigo Limited, CN=Sectigo Public Time Stamping Root R46
roots.obtained: 2026-11-07 from a Sectigo response (https://timestamp.sectigo.com, certReq=true): the chain Signer R37 -> CA R41 -> Root R46. This R46 certificate is cross-signed by USERTrust RSA Certification Authority, and `openssl verify -CAfile USERTrust_RSA_Certification_Authority.pem r46.pem` succeeds against the Mozilla/Debian trust store copy of USERTrust.
roots.check: request a token with certReq (openssl ts -query -data f -sha256 -cert | curl --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: application/timestamp-query' https://timestamp.sectigo.com), extract the certificates (openssl ts -reply -token_out; openssl pkcs7 -inform DER -print_certs), verify the Root R46 certificate against your system's USERTrust root, then compute the pin of Root R46.
